questions.question: The concept of "judicial review" in India allows the judiciary to review and strike down laws that are found to be:

options.text: Supported by a two-thirds majority in the State Legislature

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** In violation of fundamental rights**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The concept of **"judicial review"** in India allows the judiciary (mainly the Supreme Court and High Courts) to review laws and executive actions to ensure that they comply with the **Constitution of India**.
 
• If a law is found to violate the **Fundamental Rights** guaranteed under the Constitution or go beyond the constitutional provisions,
 
 
• the judiciary can declare it unconstitutional or invalid.
 
 
 
• It primarily focuses on protecting the **Fundamental Rights** of citizens and upholding the **Constitutional structure**.
 
• Judicial review can strike down any law that violates fundamental rights,
 
 
• even if it has been passed by Parliament or supported by the President or a majority in the legislature.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of judicial review in India has been borrowed from the **United States Constitution**.
 
• In the landmark case of **Marbury v. Madison (1803)**, the U.S. Supreme Court, under Chief Justice John Marshall,
 
 
• established the principle of judicial review, allowing the courts to invalidate laws that were contrary to the U.S. Constitution.
 
 
 
• This principle was incorporated into the Indian legal system during the framing of the Constitution.

questions.question: The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA) aims to provide a guarantee of how many days of employment per year to rural households in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**100**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 'The Act mandates the provision of 100 days of wage employment per year.'
 
• National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA):
 
 
• The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, now known as the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), was implemented in 2006.
 
• It aims to enhance livelihood security in rural areas by providing at least 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to every household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work.
 
• The Act was passed in September 2005 and came into effect on February 2, 2006.
 
• MGNREGA is regarded as a significant step towards the right to work and has been instrumental in addressing issues of poverty and unemployment in rural India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA), enacted in 2005, is a social security measure aimed at guaranteeing the 'right to work' in India.
 
• NREGA provides at least 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work.
 
• The primary objective of NREGA is to enhance livelihood security in rural areas by providing durable assets and strengthening the resource base of rural communities.
 
• The Act ensures transparency and accountability through measures like social audits and mandates timely payment of wages. It also includes provisions for unemployment allowance if the work is not provided within 15 days of application.
 
• NREGA is implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development and is a demand-driven scheme, meaning work is provided based on the demand from rural households.
 
• The scheme has had a significant impact on reducing rural poverty, creating rural infrastructure, and promoting inclusive growth.

• This plan includes substantial investment in iron and steel, coal and Heavy engineering, Machine building, Heavy chemicals, and Cement Industries.​
 
 
 
• ​Fourth-Five year Plan:
 
 
• ​The duration of this Plan is 1969-1974 under the leadership of Indira Gandhi.
 
• The two main objectives of this Plan are growth with Stability and Progressive achievement with self-reliance.
 
• During this Plan, 14 major Indian Banks were nationalized.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements regarding money is correct?

I. Money supply is a stock variable.

II. The total stock of money in circulation among the public at a particular point of time is called money supply.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Money supply is a stock variable**.

 
 
• **This statement is correct **because the money supply represents the total amount of money available in the economy at a specific point in time.
 
• **Stock variables are measured at a particular moment**, distinguishing them from flow variables,
 
 
• which are measured over a period of time (like income or expenditure).
 
 
 
 
 
• **The total stock of money in circulation among the public at a particular point of time is called money supply.**
 
 
• **This statement is also accurate.**
 
• The money supply includes all forms of money available to the public, such as cash, coins, and demand deposits, at a given time.
 
• It reflects the liquidity in the economy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The money supply can be broken down into different categories, such as:
 
 
• **M0**: This is the total of all physical currency (coins and notes) in circulation and is often referred to as "base money" or "monetary base."
 
• **M1**: This includes M0 plus demand deposits (checking accounts) and other liquid assets that can quickly be converted into cash.
 
• **M2**: This encompasses M1 plus savings accounts, time deposits, and other near-money assets that are less liquid than M1 components.
 
• **M3**: This includes M2 plus larger time deposits, institutional money market funds, and other larger liquid assets.
 
 
 
• Central banks use tools like open market operations, discount rates, and reserve requirements to manage the money supply.
 
 
• **Open Market Operations**: Buying or selling government bonds to increase or decrease the amount of money in circulation.
 
• **Discount Rate**: The interest rate charged to commercial banks for loans received from the central bank's discount window.
 
• **Reserve Requirements**: The minimum amount of reserves that banks must hold against deposits, affecting how much money banks can lend out.

questions.question: Into how many ages is the prehistoric times in terms of technology divided?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Three**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Prehistoric times are typically divided into **three ages** in terms of technology:
 
• **Stone Age**: This is the earliest period of human technology, characterized by the use of stone tools. It is further divided into:
 
 
• **Paleolithic (Old Stone Age)**: It is Marked by the use of simple stone tools and the development of hunter-gatherer societies.
 
• **Mesolithic (Middle Stone Age)**: It is a transitional phase with advances in tool-making and the beginnings of settled life.
 
• **Neolithic (New Stone Age)**: It is characterized by the development of agriculture, permanent settlements, and polished stone tools.
 
 
 
• **Bronze Age**: Following the Stone Age, this period saw the development of metalworking, particularly the use of bronze (an alloy of copper and tin) for tools and weapons.
 
 
• This age is marked by advancements in trade, urbanization, and social structures.
 
 
 
• **Iron Age**: This age followed the Bronze Age and is characterized by the widespread use of iron for tools and weapons.
 
 
• It brought significant advancements in agriculture, warfare, and the establishment of powerful civilizations.

Difference between Cost Price (CP) and Selling Price (SP) = Rs. 224

Loss Percentage = 40%

**Formula used:**

SP = CP × (1 - Loss Percentage / 100)

**Calculations:**

SP = CP × (1 - 0.40)

⇒ SP = CP × 0.60

CP - SP = 224

⇒ CP - (CP × 0.60) = 224

⇒ CP × (1 - 0.60) = 224

⇒ CP × 0.40 = 224

⇒ CP = 224 / 0.40

⇒ CP = 560

⇒ SP = CP × 0.60 = 560 × 0.60

⇒ SP = 336

**∴ The selling price of the table is Rs. 336.**

questions.question: Two trains are moving in the same direction at the speed of 34 km/hr and 86 km/hr, their lengths are 300 metres and 480 metres respectively. What will be the time taken by faster train to cross the slower train?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of the slower train (S1) = 34 km/hr

Speed of the faster train (S2) = 86 km/hr

Length of the slower train (L1) = 300 meters

Length of the faster train (L2) = 480 meters

**Calculations:**

1. Convert Speeds from km/hr to m/s:

⇒ Speed in m/s = Speed in km/hr × (5/18)

⇒ Speed of slower train (S1):

⇒ S1 = 34 × (5/18) = 170/18 = 85/9 m/s

⇒ Speed of faster train (S2):

⇒ S2 = 86 × (5/18) = 430/18 = 215/9 m/s

2. Relative Speed:

⇒ Relative Speed = S2 - S1

⇒ = (215/9) - (85/9) = (215 - 85) / 9 = 130/9 m/s

3. Total Length to be Crossed:

⇒ Total Length = L1 + L2 = 300 + 480 = 780 meters

4. Time Taken to Cross:

⇒ Time = Distance / Speed

⇒ Time = 780 / (130/9)

⇒ = 780 × (9/130)

⇒ = (780 × 9) / 130

⇒ = 7020 / 130 = 54 seconds

**∴ The time taken by the faster train to cross the slower train is 54 seconds.**

⇒ A = P + SI

⇒ SI = A - P = 5P - P = 4P

⇒ SI = P × R × T / 100

⇒ 4P = P × R × 8 / 100

⇒ 4 = R × 8 / 100

⇒ R = 4 × 100 / 8 = 50%

⇒ SI in 24 years = P × R × T / 100

⇒ SI = P × 12
